A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NoisyCLIP research despite the changed title and format. Their methods, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original alignment, Best-of-N, factual-consistency, ablation, and qualitative results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds LatentCLIP comparisons, cross-architecture evaluations, and a human preference study.

M1.justification: The contrastive objective, frozen text encoder, and training interval 20–29 remain unchanged. v2 adds an inference adaptation for DiT inputs: model-specific VAE decoding replaces the linear latent-to-RGB conversion used for SDXL (Section 4.5).

E1.justification: v2 extends evaluation from SDXL-generated representations to zero-shot transfer on SD3.5 and FLUX.1 [dev] trajectories, testing substantially different latent input distributions (Section 5.4). The two caption benchmarks remain, and renaming factual consistency as latent-to-text retrieval does not introduce another task.

E2.justification: LatentCLIP-8 and LatentCLIP-4-plus become evaluated comparators in the main Best-of-N experiments and Appendix C tables. LatentCLIP also enters qualitative comparisons. v1 cited LatentCLIP but evaluated primarily frozen CLIP and SigLIP, so this materially strengthens comparator coverage.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a blind preference protocol using 100 randomly sampled GenAI-Bench Basic image pairs, comparing selections at latent step 20 and excluding strict ties (Appendix C.3). New DiT experiments use zero-shot evaluation, VAE decoding, and shorter generation schedules, including 28 steps. Existing SDXL training and benchmark settings are retained.

E4.justification: Section 5.4 adds tests of robustness to changing the generating architecture, and Appendix C.3 independently checks automatic evaluation through human preferences. Appendix F expands and revises failure examples with LatentCLIP. Training-range, encoder-training, and model-size ablations already existed in v1 and are retained.

E5.justification: The new human study reports inter-rater agreement, κ = 0.724, adding a statistical reliability assessment absent from v1. Neither version reports confidence intervals or repeated-training-run variability; the revision does not establish increased replication.

E6.justification: v2 adds LatentCLIP scores, DiT alignment-versus-cost curves, and 61.3% human preference for NoisyCLIP among non-tied trials. Existing Table 1 and encoder-ablation scores remain unchanged. It also replaces some qualitative selections and removes the dedicated latent-30 Best-of-N panel and Appendix C average-gap columns.

T1.justification: The definition accompanying Equation 3 relaxes Φ from a linear transformation to a general transformation, consistent with the added VAE decoding. Equations 1–3 otherwise retain their mathematical form, and no theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: v1's abstract claims 98% of CLIP performance at half cost; v2 strengthens this to matching or beating full-cost frozen CLIP. The introduction also extends the efficiency claim across multiple architectures. The central NoisyCLIP, benchmark, and early-stopping contributions remain.

C2.justification: v1 treats NoisySigLIP's weaker retrieval performance as limited transfer across backbones. v2 attributes it to sigmoid-versus-softmax discrimination and emphasizes robust transfer for visual selection (Section 5.4). It also interprets the new DiT results as architectural transfer and revises failure-case explanations in Appendix F.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page address where v1 only promised future code and data, and documents DiT VAE decoding and shorter generation schedules. Core training hyperparameters and hardware remain unchanged. The PDFs alone do not establish whether the linked resources are actually available.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to FLUX.1 Kontext, SANA 1.5, and b-CLIP. It sharpens positioning against the already-cited LatentCLIP by emphasizing early noisy-latent ranking rather than final-stage superiority. The related-work survey is otherwise largely retained.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled, the abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten around three challenges, and the results narrative is reorganized. Factual consistency becomes latent-to-text retrieval within alignment analysis, while training-range analysis moves ahead of Best-of-N and backbone discussion becomes generalization analysis.

P2.justification: v2 changes from two-column to single-column layout, extends Figure 1 with an early-stopping schematic, redesigns alignment plots, adds DiT plots and LatentCLIP rows, and expands qualitative grids. The combined appendix benchmark table becomes separate Basic and Advanced tables, and the latent-30 Best-of-N panel is removed.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical validation by addressing v1's missing latent-specialized comparison and SDXL-only, automatic evaluation through LatentCLIP tests, cross-architecture transfer, and human preferences. These additions make the central efficiency argument more credible. The stronger abstract overstates the retained SDXL results, which still report a small drop against full-cost CLIP, and the human study lacks annotator counts and uncertainty estimates. These shortcomings limit, but do not outweigh, the substantial evidential gains.
